findings.title: Oversized request path destroys the socket without handling the resulting aborted/error event
findings.evidence: When the body exceeds the cap, the middleware sends a 413 and immediately calls req.destroy(), but it only listens for req.on('error') and never handles the aborted/close path that destroy commonly triggers on IncomingMessage. In Node this can surface as an unhandled stream error or leave the request lifecycle in an undefined state after a response has already been written.
findings.recommendation: Do not destroy the request without also handling the resulting termination events safely. Prefer stopping further processing by removing listeners and draining/ignoring the rest of the body, or add explicit handling for aborted/close and ensure no unhandled error is emitted after sending the 413.

findings.title: Content-Type check accepts non-JSON types that merely share the prefix
findings.evidence: The gate uses a simple prefix test, so values like application/jsonp or application/json-seq will pass even though they are not standard JSON request bodies for JSON.parse.
findings.recommendation: Parse the media type token and require an exact match for application/json, optionally also allowing structured syntax suffixes such as application/*+json if intended.
